answer.origin: New York Post reporting an NVIDIA and OpenAI announcement dated 2026-08-17; NVIDIA’s same-day SEC filing (e1205–e1212) supplies the binding-agreement details.
answer.note: The companies’ announcement was reported as NVIDIA providing up to $105 billion in financing toward OpenAI’s Ohio data center. NVIDIA’s filing clarifies that this is a cumulative cap on its initial commitment under residual-value guaranties with SB Energy, not an unconditional $105 billion payment or a guarantee of all project costs. The agreements cover leases for approximately 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site, where OpenAI is the tenant. If OpenAI becomes insolvent and defaults or fails to pay rent, NVIDIA may owe SB Energy a defined shortfall, subject to the agreements’ conditions; OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid. The guaranties generally take effect when the relevant leases commence, with ready-for-service conditions expected to begin in 2028; NVIDIA says exposure declines as capacity comes online and OpenAI pays rent, with phased effect between 2028 and 2030. This is a signed, material contingent obligation and supports a yes for the lease-guarantee question, but not a claim that NVIDIA guarantees all lease or debt financing. OpenAI’s planned deployment of NVIDIA’s DSX platform at the site indicates potential customer use and demand, not disclosed GPU orders or revenue. Actual exposure and demand realization depend on lease conditions, deployment, and OpenAI’s performance.
limitations: The $105 billion is a cap on NVIDIA’s initial aggregate guaranty commitment, not the expected amount paid; actual exposure and any payments are not disclosed here.
The filing describes conditions and a phased commencement, but the relevant leases’ actual start dates and whether ready-for-service conditions have been met remain unknown.
The announcement and filing do not quantify NVIDIA product orders, purchase timing, or revenue from OpenAI’s planned DSX deployment.
follow_up: Review subsequent NVIDIA filings for guaranty exposure, payments, or changes to the $105 billion cap, and SB Energy lease commencement and ready-for-service status.
Check later project updates for capacity entering service from 2028 onward and whether OpenAI is making the related lease payments.
Check NVIDIA disclosures and OpenAI or project updates for actual product orders and deployment, distinguishing those from planned use of the DSX platform.

updates.statement: Yes. On 2026-08-17 NVIDIA entered into residual-value guaranties with SB Energy for leases covering approximately 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site, where OpenAI is the tenant. The filing states that NVIDIA’s aggregate payment obligation under its initial commitment is capped at $105 billion and describes payments tied to specified OpenAI lease-default events, subject to conditions. This establishes a signed binding guarantee for the data-center lease by the deadline, although it is not a guarantee of all project costs or debt financing. The guaranties generally become effective when the applicable leases commence, and specified ready-for-service conditions are expected to begin in 2028. (incoming; e1205–e1210)
limitations: The disclosed guaranty is conditional and lease-related; it does not establish a guarantee of all project costs or debt financing.
Actual lease commencement, conditions being met, and any amount paid under the guaranties are not established.
what_would_change_it: A subsequent filing or authoritative agreement showing the guaranties were not effective, were terminated, or did not cover an OpenAI data-center lease would change the conclusion.
